question.worked_solution:
Let $u={x}^{2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=2x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int \operatorname{sin}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{sin}⁡u\cdot \frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡u\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡u+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}^{2})+C\end{aligned}
$$
